conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Patel. I'll be your doctor during your stay. You were brought in because your blood sugar was extremely high. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, last night my glucose monitor said 'does not register.' It's been running between 200 and 500 since I left the hospital a couple of weeks ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You’re on Lantus at bedtime and Humalog with meals, correct? Any changes to your diet or medications?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No changes. I’m still taking everything the same. I’ve been eating okay, maybe a bit more since I started Megace for my appetite.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That might be part of the issue. Megace can make your body more resistant to insulin, which raises blood sugar. We also saw your kidney function is a bit worse than usual.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My kidneys again? They’ve always been bad since the transplant.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your creatinine is 2.2, up from your usual 1.5. But it improved to 1.6 after fluids in the ER. This looks like it’s due to dehydration from high sugars causing you to urinate a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, I have been going to the bathroom a lot. I thought it was the Megace.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It could be both. High glucose spills into the urine and pulls water with it. That also explains why your potassium was high at first — your kidneys weren’t clearing it well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that dangerous? My potassium?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It was 7.2 initially, which is concerning, but it corrected to 5.5 after fluids and no EKG changes. It’s now normal. So we’re watching it, but it’s improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. What about my insulin? I don’t want to go into a coma or anything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No signs of ketoacidosis or coma. You’re alert and your labs don’t show that. But we do need to adjust your insulin. The endocrine team recommends increasing your Lantus from 3 units to 10 units at bedtime.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a big jump! Won’t I go low?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor closely. You’ve been running very high, so this is to bring you into a safer range. We’ll also adjust your Humalog sliding scale to give more insulin when your sugar is high.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. And what about the Megace? I finally have an appetite.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to cut it in half — from 20 mL to 10 mL daily. It’s likely contributing to the insulin resistance. We’ll see how your appetite does on the lower dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I can try that. Will I lose weight again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll watch that. The transplant team will help manage your nutrition. For now, the priority is getting your sugars under control safely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your fingerstick this morning is 385. Still high, but we expected that. We’ve increased your Lantus to 10 units last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s not dropping fast, is it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It takes a few days to stabilize. Your A1c was 7.3%, which shows your average sugar has been high over the last few months. We’re on the right track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been trying. It’s just hard with all these meds and my stomach issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’re keeping your other medications the same — tacrolimus, mycophenolate, mirtazapine for depression and appetite, and your blood pressure medicine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Doctor, I just checked my sugar — it’s 410. Should I take extra Humalog?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, according to your new sliding scale, you should take 8 units of Humalog now. We’ve adjusted the scale to be more aggressive.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll do that. I’m just worried I’m not doing enough.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great. This is a process. Your sugars will come down as the new doses take effect. We’re also watching your kidney function and electrolytes daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Your labs look better. Creatinine is down to 1.6, potassium is 4.9, and your glucose this morning was 290 — still high, but trending down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good! Is the new insulin working?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s starting to. We’ll keep the Lantus at 10 units and further adjust your Humalog scale today to help with mealtime spikes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the half-dose Megace? I’m still eating okay so far.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great news. The transplant team wants you to keep it at 10 mL and follow up with them to monitor your intake and weight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Doctor, I feel much better. My sugars are staying around 280-300. Is that okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s improving. We’d like to see it under 200 eventually, but this is progress. Your kidney function is stable, and you’re not having any symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news — you’re ready to go home today. Your sugars are more stable, and your labs are improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great! What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue the new insulin: 10 units Lantus at bedtime, and use the updated Humalog sliding scale. Take half your Megace — 10 mL daily. Keep all your other meds the same.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my follow-ups?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: See the endocrine clinic tomorrow, your transplant team soon, and we’ll help you set up with a new primary care doctor. You’re doing well — just keep monitoring your sugars.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel much more in control now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Call if your sugars go too high or too low. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up.
